forecast-period.text: A ridge of high pressure to the east directs a northerly flow over South Australia. A trough and cold front about the far west will cross the state today and Monday morning. A cool southwesterly airstream will follow as a new high drifts eastwards across the Bight early this week.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Showers and thunderstorms in the northwest, extending to central and eastern parts during the day. Thunderstorms possibly severe with damaging winds, large hail and heavy rain which may lead to flash flooding. Possible early morning fog patches about the southeast. Maximum temperatures above average. Northeast to northwesterly winds, fresh in the north and west, ahead of a south to southwesterly change moving into the far west during the afternoon and extending across the agricultural areas by the evening.

Isolated to scattered showers and possible thunderstorms continue across central and eastern districts early, contracting northeast throughout the day. Showers and thunderstorms continue in the northwest. Thunderstorms possibly severe with damaging winds. Maximum temperatures below average in the east, grading to well below average in the west. North to northwesterly winds in the far north, ahead of south to southwesterly change extending across the state and freshening near the coast.

Chance of isolated light morning showers about the southern agricultural area Isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms continue in the north and northwest. Maximum temperatures below to well below average. South to southeasterly winds, fresh at times in the northeast and tending southwest to southerly about the southern agricultural area.

text.p: Chance of isolated light morning showers about the southern agricultural area. Isolated to scattered showers and possible thunderstorms in the northwest, extending into central parts and gradually moving to the northeast. Maximum temperatures below to well below average. East to southeasterly winds.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Wednesday: Broadly 2 to 10 mm across the pastoral districts, increasing 20 to 40 mm in the far north. 5 to 10 mm about the agricultural areas, with isolated higher falls of 15 to 25 mm possible. Localised falls of 40 to 50 mm are possible with severe thunderstorms.
